To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) We develop a novel model for multi task learning that allows for the presence of shared parameters and also allows for the possibility of non-shared parameters.

(i) the dirty model is a simple but effective way to leverage the benefits of parameter overlap, (ii) it strictly outperforms both block l1 and l1 regularization, (iii) it works under high dimensional scaling, (iv) the performance is robust to varying degrees of overlap, (v) it can also be applied to other dirty structured settings such as low rank + sparse, (vi) the performance can be further improved by a careful choice of regularization parameter
1) We develop a dirty model for multiple regression, which allows us to leverage parameter overlap, but not pay for it when it is not there.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of learning from data with dirty structures, where we do not know a priori whether the data is block sparse, low rank, or some other neat structure, but we know that it is not all of one neat type.
developing a new dirty model to handle multi task learning problems where the extent of overlap of relevant features is unknown, but where we can still exploit it when it does exist.
the development of new statistical estimation techniques for dirty data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a generalization of the l1/lq block sparse model.
the method proposed in this paper is the most robust and performs the best across all possible scenarios, and hence can be used as a default method for multi-task learning.
we propose and develop the Dirty Model, a new method for Multi task learning, which outperforms the best of existing methods, in all settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new method for multi task learning, that works well even when the tasks have very different features.
we develop a new dirty model which can leverage the overlap of relevant features across tasks, even if their values are different.

we propose an efficient method to estimate the parameters for a multi-task learning problem where the set of relevant variables is different for each of the tasks and the parameters of the common variables may or may not be similar for the different tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can develop dirty models for high dimensional problems, which can outperform existing methods, without any knowledge about the true parameter.
it is important to develop tools for dirty data, where we can leverage the information in the overlap when it is there, but not penalize for the absence of it.
it is important to consider dirty models, and that we can do so by leveraging simple ideas.
